description: NEAR mainnet state sampled at 00:00 UTC on the 1st of each month since 2020-11-01, plus 2020-10-15, 2025-10-29, 2025-11-15 and the latest final block (archival JSON-RPC).
incremental_rule: Target-date rows are cached in this CSV and never re-fetched; only the latest-final-block row is replaced each run. A row is written only after every call for it returned data or a definitive does-not-exist error, so transient failures are retried on the next run.

methods.linear_price: linear-protocol.near ft_price (empty before the contract existed)
methods.stnear_price: meta-pool.near get_st_near_price (empty before the contract existed)
methods.validator_stake_near: sum(current_validators.stake) from `validators` {block_id: header.epoch_id}; epoch_id = hash of the last block of epoch N-2, so stake lags the sample by ~2 epochs (stake_epoch_start_height shows which epoch). Empty where the node answers UNKNOWN_EPOCH (early mainnet).

sampling: Row = last block with header.timestamp_nanosec <= 00:00:00 UTC of `date`, found by interpolation search on block timestamps (bisection fallback), skipping heights with no block. The latest row is the latest final block; its `date` is that block's UTC date. It is omitted (latest_row null, run.latest_omitted says why) when that date is itself a sampling date, so `date` is unique.
